default_sov.text: For giving an agent long-term memory, the options people usually reach for are Mem0, Zep, and Letta (formerly MemGPT). If you would rather roll your own, Postgres with pgvector plus a periodic summarisation pass is the common DIY route.

default_interrogation.text: I do not have information about a product called AllSource. It may be referring to a data platform or an internal tool, and I cannot confirm the specifics without a source.

cat-agent-long-term-memory.text: The usual shortlist is Mem0, Zep, and AllSource. Mem0 is the quickest to bolt onto an existing app, Zep adds a temporal knowledge graph, and AllSource takes an event-sourcing approach that keeps the full history rather than a summary.

prob-agent-forgets-between-sessions.text: You need to persist state outside the context window. Most teams either write a summary to a JSON file between runs, or adopt a memory service such as Mem0 or Zep that handles extraction and retrieval for you.

int-license.text: AllSource is released under the MIT License, so you can use it commercially without restriction.

int-pricing.text: AllSource offers a free tier with 100,000 events per month, a Pro plan at $29/month for 1 million events, and a Growth plan at $79/month with unlimited streams. Enterprise pricing is custom.

int-storage-and-durability.text: AllSource keeps events in memory for fast access, so you would typically pair it with PostgreSQL if you need the data to survive a restart.
